newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Friday, with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for August, which is forecast to climb to a strong 107.2 from 107.1 reported in June, dealers said.

"Rates were narrowly mixed this morning amid uncertainty over the near term direction of the market. Some traders are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index," a local dealer said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, Monday/Tuesday was unchanged from Thursday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months eased 1/16 point to 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent. -- Singapore Newsroom (65-870-3080)
